title: School identity
content: The official name is Jain Heritage School Electronic City, also referred to as JHS Electronic City. It is a member of the JGI Group and is located in Rayasandra near Electronic City in Bengaluru.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, About Us

title: Grades and curriculum
content: Jain Heritage School Electronic City currently presents programmes from Playgroup through Grade 7. Pre-Primary includes Playgroup, Nursery, LKG and UKG. Grades 1 through 7 are offered with a choice of CBSE or ICSE. The official website says the campus plans to add one grade each academic year, beginning with Grade 8 in 2028-29 and reaching Grade 12 in 2032-33.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions and Grades 1-7

title: Boards offered
content: The Electronic City campus offers both CBSE and ICSE. Families choose the board during the application and enrolment process, not when first submitting an enquiry. The school offers a board consultation during the campus visit to help families compare the two pathways.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions

title: CBSE pathway
content: The school's CBSE pathway is described as NCERT-aligned and structured under the NEP 2020 5+3+3+4 framework. The official website highlights Mathematics and Science foundations, competency-based learning, national portability and later alignment with examinations such as JEE, NEET and CUET. The school states that it teaches the full CBSE syllabus using Finnish-inspired methods.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, CBSE

title: ICSE pathway
content: The school's ICSE pathway follows the CISCE curriculum. The official website describes it as language-rich and analytically focused, with English, a second language, Mathematics, Environmental Science or Science, Social Studies, Computer Applications, Value Education, Art and Craft, and Physical Education among the learning areas for Grades 1 through 7.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, ICSE

title: Early-years learning approach
content: Pre-Primary covers Playgroup, Nursery, LKG and UKG and is described for approximately ages 2.5 to 5. The programme uses purposeful play, guided exploration, storytelling, art, movement, outdoor activity and reflection. Through play, children practise language, motor skills, cooperation, spatial reasoning, problem-solving and early scientific thinking. Published age bands are indicative; exact admission eligibility must be confirmed by the admissions team.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Pre-Primary

title: Pre-Primary daily rhythm
content: The Pre-Primary page describes a flexible daily rhythm rather than fixed published clock times. Activities include settling and free choice, circle time, guided exploration, a shared snack, outdoor gross-motor play, quiet or mindfulness time, creative activity and reflection before going home.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Pre-Primary

title: Finnish and Nordic-inspired methodology
content: The school combines the requirements of CBSE or ICSE with Finnish-inspired teaching practices. It says it adopts Finnish practices that fit its students and the applicable board framework rather than copying the Finnish system in full. The approach emphasizes inquiry, understanding, application, collaboration, reflection, differentiated instruction and independent thinking. The official brochure also describes early education as influenced by Montessori and Reggio Emilia philosophies.
source_label: JHS official website, Philosophy and Why JHS; official brochure, pages 2-3

title: Learning and assessment in Grades 1-7
content: For Grades 1 through 7, the school describes visual, auditory and kinesthetic learning routes. Each child has an individual learning portfolio. Day-to-day assessment includes observation, discussion, reflective journals, peer assessment and self-assessment, while formal assessment includes projects, presentations and unit tests. The school says it does not publish a rank order for children.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Grades 1-7

title: Educational philosophy
content: The school's published vision is to encourage human development through ethical values, character-building, leadership and education. It emphasizes social responsibility, critical thinking, cultural heritage and the intellectual, moral, physical, social and emotional development of each child. The school describes education as preparation for life, not only examinations.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, About Us

title: Campus learning spaces
content: The campus website describes STEAM and robotics facilities, a library and reading spaces, art, music and performance rooms, a Discovery Zone, a Manipulative Learning Centre and a Contemplative Learning Centre. The Manipulative Learning Centre supports hands-on learning with concrete materials, while the Contemplative Learning Centre supports reflection, journals and self-assessment.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Campus

title: Sports facilities
content: The school's public information describes sports and physical education as part of the timetable, with fitness, teamwork, discipline and healthy competition among its aims. The official brochure additionally lists basketball, volleyball, table tennis, badminton, swimming, cricket practice nets, futsal and indoor games.
source_label: JHS official website, Why JHS; official brochure, page 4

title: Library, yoga, dance and music
content: The school describes a library and reading culture together with dedicated spaces and timetabled opportunities for art, music and performance. The official brochure also lists yoga, mindfulness, dance and music programmes.
source_label: JHS official website, Campus and Why JHS; official brochure, page 4

title: School meal plan
content: The school states that meals are designed by qualified dieticians and cooked on campus. Meals are optional for Pre-Primary. The official brochure identifies Sodexo as the meal-service partner. Allergy and dietary needs are recorded during admission and are intended to be followed by the school.
source_label: JHS official website, Admissions and Campus; official brochure, page 4

title: Transport and extended day care
content: The school website states that school transport with pick-up and drop is available, along with extended day care for families needing a longer day. Transport pricing depends on the family's address and route. Route coverage, timings, availability and charges must be confirmed with the admissions team for the family's specific location.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Campus and Admissions

title: Admission process
content: The published admission process has four stages: enquire by submitting interest online or calling the school; visit the campus and consult the team; complete the application, choose CBSE or ICSE and provide the required documents; then attend an age-appropriate interaction followed by an admission offer and onboarding when applicable.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions

title: Admission enquiry information
content: For an initial admission enquiry, the website asks for the child's name and date of birth, the grade being considered and a contact number. Families may instead call the admissions team at +91 96630 21118. The website says a counsellor calls to answer questions and arrange a visit.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions

title: Pre-Primary admission interaction
content: The school states that there is no entrance test for Pre-Primary. Instead, it conducts a friendly, age-appropriate interaction intended to help the school understand how the child learns. Transfer and mid-year admissions for other grades are handled case by case and should be discussed with admissions.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions

title: Admission eligibility and age
content: The website presents Pre-Primary as approximately ages 2.5 to 5 and Grades 1 through 7 as approximately ages 6 to 13. These age bands are indicative. Exact date-of-birth cut-offs, grade eligibility, transfer eligibility and exceptions must be confirmed by the admissions team for the relevant academic session.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions and Pre-Primary

title: Fee information policy
content: The school does not publish exact fee amounts on its website. It says the complete current structure is shared directly and may include grade-specific tuition, meals, transport priced by route and distance, books, materials, uniform, available discounts or concessions, and extended day care. Families can request the current figures from admissions before visiting. Exact amounts must be confirmed directly with the school.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions

title: Seat availability
content: The admissions page says seats in each section are limited and encourages families to begin early. It does not publish live seat counts. Availability for a particular grade, board and academic session must be confirmed by the admissions team.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions

title: Enquiry privacy statement
content: The school's public website says enquiry details go to its admissions team, are not sold or shared, and are not added to a marketing mailing list or automated follow-up campaign. The admissions process page says the school makes one call to answer questions and offer a visit slot.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Admissions

title: School contact details and location
content: Jain Heritage School Electronic City is located at Sy No 22/2 and 25/2, Rayasandra Main Road, Rayasandra, Bengaluru, Sriramapura, Karnataka 560099. The admissions phone number is +91 96630 21118 and the email address is info@jhselectroniccity.com. The official website is https://jhselectroniccity.com/. Campus visits should be booked in advance.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Contact

title: JGI Group background
content: Jain Heritage School belongs to the JGI Group. The official website identifies Dr. Chenraj Roychand as the Founder and Chairman of the JGI Group and says he founded the group in 1990. The group has more than 100 institutions in its network. The Electronic City campus describes a pathway extending from school to JAIN colleges and JAIN (Deemed-to-be University). The website states his chairmanship at the JGI Group level rather than naming a separate chairman specifically for the Electronic City campus.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, About Us and Admissions

title: Chairman's educational message
content: The official About page carries a message from Dr. Chenraj Roychand, identified as Founder and Chairman of the JGI Group. The message says education should be for life rather than only for earning a living, and describes the school's role as recognizing each child's strengths, protecting their curiosity and helping them build confidence. This is a JGI Group leadership message; the page does not identify a separate Electronic City campus chairman.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, About Us

title: K-12 learning continuum
content: The school's published learning continuum has four stages: Exploration in Pre-Primary, Foundation in Grades 1 through 7, Formation in middle school and Direction in high school. The Electronic City campus currently publishes programmes through Grade 7 and says later grades will open progressively, so descriptions of the later stages explain the planned pathway rather than classes currently available at every level.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Philosophy

title: School-wide learning cycle
content: Across the school, the published learning path moves through five steps: wonder, experience, work together, reflect and apply. The school describes this as a cross-stage method used with age-appropriate differences in Pre-Primary and Grades 1 through 7. It is a teaching method layered onto the selected CBSE or ICSE syllabus, not a replacement board or separate curriculum.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Philosophy and Why JHS

title: Personalised learning and student support
content: The website says teachers recognise visual, auditory and kinesthetic learning routes, record learning-style observations and use differentiated instruction. It describes targeted support for children who need more time and says learning information is carried forward to the next teacher. The school publishes a staff-to-student ratio of 1:15. These statements describe the school's general approach and do not guarantee an individual diagnosis, therapy or specific accommodation without confirmation from the school.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Philosophy, Why JHS and Grades 1-7

title: Multiple intelligences and transversal competences
content: The school says it deliberately develops eight forms of intelligence: linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal and naturalistic. It also says seven transversal competences are integrated into subjects and everyday learning rather than taught only as a separate life-skills period.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Philosophy and Pre-Primary

title: Arts, communication and leadership
content: The school describes visual arts, vocal and instrumental music, dance, drama, assemblies and productions as timetabled parts of learning rather than optional extras. It says circle time, student responsibilities, presentations and stage opportunities are used to build public speaking, expression, confidence and leadership progressively.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Why JHS

title: Enterprise and real-world skills
content: The website describes a Budding Entrepreneur Programme in which children practise developing ideas, planning, budgeting, creating and presenting. It places enterprise, initiative, collaboration and real-world problem-solving within the broader school programme rather than treating them only as occasional events.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Why JHS

title: Student wellbeing, health and safety
content: The school's public pages describe attentive supervision, secure campus protocols, mindfulness, empathy education, pastoral support and wellbeing as parts of school life. They also describe monitored transport, safe play areas, nutritious meals and extended day care. The website does not publish operational details of security procedures; specific medical, accessibility, allergy, safeguarding or emergency requirements should be confirmed directly with the school.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Why JHS and Campus

title: Choosing between CBSE and ICSE
content: The school presents CBSE and ICSE as equal pathways using the same campus infrastructure, shared community and Finnish-inspired teaching approach. Its published guidance describes CBSE as structured, NCERT-aligned and nationally portable, while ICSE is described as broad, language-rich and analytically focused. Academic counsellors offer a board consultation based on a child's learning style, strengths and family aspirations. The school advises choosing for fit rather than treating either board as universally better.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, CBSE and ICSE

title: Campus status and published facilities
content: The official campus page says the Rayasandra Electronic City campus is open for Playgroup through Grade 7 and is designed to grow to Grade 12. It lists STEAM and robotics labs, learning centres, library and reading areas, arts and performance spaces, and sports and movement areas. The page also discloses that some photographs may show the facilities standard at other operating Jain Heritage School campuses while Electronic City-specific photography is being completed; families can confirm the exact current facilities during a booked campus visit.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Campus

title: Contact hours and visit booking
content: The Contact page publishes office hours as Monday to Saturday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and says email replies are normally made within one working day. Campus visits should be booked in advance so a staff member is available. Some website footers display campus hours as 9:30 AM to 5:00 PM, so visitors should call +91 96630 21118 before travelling if the opening time matters.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Contact

title: Careers and job applications
content: The careers page covers teaching, administration, information technology, finance, creative and support roles across the Electronic City, Whitefield and Hebbal campuses, with full-time and part-time filters. Openings can change and should be checked on the live careers page. When no suitable role is listed, the page invites applicants to send a resume to info@jhselectroniccity.com. Recruitment enquiries are handled through the careers route rather than the admissions process.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Careers

title: Published admissions session
content: The official website currently advertises admissions for the 2027-28 academic session for Playgroup through Grade 7. This is a time-sensitive website notice, not proof of a live seat in a particular class or board. The current intake year, deadline and seat availability must be confirmed on the live admissions page or with the admissions team before a family acts on it.
source_label: JHS Electronic City official website, Home and Admissions
